evals.prompt: Write a 30-second UGC ad script for a skincare serum, from the perspective of a customer who was skeptical at first.
evals.expected_output: Should follow the UGC structure: hook, problem, discovery/turn, demo/proof, objection handle, CTA. Should use the skeptic-to-believer angle explicitly. Should write in casual, contraction-heavy spoken language, not brand copy. Should include a text-overlay track distinct from the spoken line and a specific, low-friction CTA.
assertions: Casual spoken language, not ad copy

evals.prompt: We need this UGC ad performed by an AI avatar instead of a real creator. Does that change anything?
evals.expected_output: Should note the script structure stays the same but flag that avatar delivery needs to sound natural/conversational since lip-sync avatars can feel stilted with brand-speak. Should suggest keeping sentences short and avoiding real-creator-only elements like handheld camera imperfections. Should cross-reference that AI avatar generation itself is a separate concern from script writing.
assertions: Confirms core script structure is unchanged
Flags natural/conversational language for avatar delivery
Notes handheld/authenticity cues don't apply the same way to avatars
